report.summary: All four failures are timeouts on pages that render the book list, and they share one cause: the app's slow_list bug adds a random 0-8 s delay to list_books, which is longer than the 5 s Playwright timeout about 37% of the time. Classify them as flaky and fix the app's timing (or stop enabling slow_list in tests) before touching any test code. One caveat: the CI workflow does not set BUGS, so first confirm the failing run actually had slow_list enabled.

causes.title: Random list_books delay pushes page loads and form submits past the 5 s Playwright timeout
causes.explanation: app/main.py:160-161 sleeps random.uniform(0, 8) before every book listing when the slow_list bug is enabled. list_books is called on GET /books (books_page -> render_books, main.py:270) and again on the error re-render of POST /books (main.py:349). The conftest sets page.set_default_timeout(5000) (tests/ui/conftest.py:7). So a page.goto('/books') or a click that waits for the redirect to /books fails whenever the random delay exceeds about 5 s. The failures match this pattern: the two goto('/books') tests timed out while waiting for the 'load' event, and the two clicks timed out on 'waiting for scheduled navigations to finish', which is the POST redirect to /books that then renders the list. The test that does reach the page without a timeout (test_future_year_shows_error_and_keeps_input's goto) and the passing test_deleted_book_disappears show the same test code passing on other draws. The app behaviour itself is correct (blank_title and year_off_by_one are not involved, and the year test never reached its assertions), so this is timing, not a product bug. The fix is to remove or bound the delay in the app (or set BUGS without slow_list for the UI suite), and to wait for the specific response rather than rely on a 5 s default. Also worth checking why this run had slow_list enabled: the workflow in .github/workflows/tests.yml does not set BUGS, and the traceback paths point to a local Windows machine.
evidence: tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:10 / tests/support/pages.py:34: Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. Call log: navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:49391/books", waiting until "load" (test_added_book_is_listed)
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:23: Page.goto: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:49392/books", waiting until "load" (test_book_created_through_api_shows_in_ui)

tests/support/pages.py:44 (BooksPage.add click): Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded ... click action done / waiting for scheduled navigations to finish (test_future_year_shows_error_and_keeps_input)

tests/ui/test_login_ui.py:9 / tests/support/pages.py:22: Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded ... waiting for scheduled navigations to finish (test_new_user_lands_on_empty_bookshelf, submit leads to /register -> redirect /books)
app/main.py:159-161: def list_books(user_id): if "slow_list" in BUGS: time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8))
app/main.py:11-12 docstring: slow_list  random 0-8 s delay when listing books (flaky timing)
app/main.py:270: "books": list_books(user["id"]) inside render_books, used by GET /books and by POST /books error path (main.py:349)
.github/workflows/tests.yml:35: pytest -m ${{ matrix.suite }} -n auto ... (no BUGS env set in workflow)
tests/ui/test_books_ui.py:38-46: the future-year test's assertions were never reached, so there is no evidence of the year_off_by_one defect here
causes.suggested_fix: 1) Confirm whether BUGS=slow_list was set for this run (the CI workflow does not set it; the paths in the traceback are from a Windows workstation). 2) If it was, do not run the UI suite with slow_list; set BUGS only in the place that needs it, or drop slow_list from the default test environment. 3) Otherwise remove the random sleep from list_books in app/main.py. 4) Make the UI tests less sensitive to latency: raise the timeout for navigations or wait on the response (page.expect_navigation / expect_response) instead of relying on the 5 s default. 5) Keep a dedicated test that exercises slow_list with a longer timeout, if the bug is meant to be detected.
